problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -10 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
feedback.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{31}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -10 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}.$
